newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken proposes J.Wallenberg as new MD.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken proposes J.Wallenberg as new MD.

text.p: Sweden's S-E-Banken said on Tuesday that managing director Bjorn Svedberg was to leave his position from April 29 with Jacob Wallenberg proposed as his replacement.
The bank said in a statement that Svedberg would leave at the annual general meeting on April 29 when his five year contract expires in order to devote all his time to industrial board work.
"The board of directors has proposed Jacob Wallenberg, at present deputy managing director of the bank, as Bjorn Svedberg's successor," the bank said in a statement.
Wallenberg, 41, has worked for the bank since 1984 except for a short break and said it would be a privilege and a challenge to head the bank.
"S-E-Banken has a strong position to cultivate and develop further," Wallenberg said in the statement.
S-E-Banken's chairman, Karl-Erik Sahlberg, said Svedberg's contribution has been very important.
"He leaves the bank after it achieved its best result ever," the statement said.
Wallenberg is part of the powerful Swedish family that controls about 18 percent of S-E-Banken.
The bank said it will hold a news conference in Stockholm at 1330 GMT on Tuesday.
